source_text:
Ἀλλ' ὡς φύλαξ ἄγρυπνον ἔχων τὸν
τῆς ψυχῆς ὀφθαλμὸν, μὴ συγχωρήσῃς τῷ λῃστῇ τὸν τῆς διανοίας διαῤῥῆξαι
ὀφθαλμὸν, ἵνα θαῤῥῶν πρὸς αὐτὸν εἴπῃς· ∆εσποτικοῦ κτήματος προδότης οὐ

γίνομαι, διάβολε. Τοῦ Κυρίου γὰρ ἡ γῆ καὶ ἡ Ἐκκλησία τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἡ πάντοτε ὑπὸ
τοῦ οὐρανίου ὄμβρου γεωργουμένη, καὶ ἀειθαλὲς καρποφοροῦσα Χριστῷ τριάκοντα
[καὶ ἑξήκοντα] καὶ ἑκατόν. Ἐξῆλθε, φησὶν, ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπεῖραι· καὶ τὸ μὲν ἔπεσεν
ἐπὶ τὴν ὁδὸν, τὴν ἀπάτην τὴν Ἑλληνικήν. Καὶ ἦλθον τὰ πετεινὰ, οἱ ὀξύπεινοι τῶν
δαιμόνων ἅρπαγες, καὶ κατέφαγον αὐτό. Ἄλλο ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη, τὴν
σκληρότροπον τῶν Ἰουδαίων φημὶ προαίρεσιν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέτειλε 43.485
προπετείας φυτὸν [καὶ] παρανομίας. Τοιοῦτος γὰρ Ἰουδαίων ὁ τρόπος. Ἐν γὰρ τῇ
ἐρήμῳ νομοθετούμενοι ἔφασκον πρὸς Μωϋσῆν· Πάντα ὅσα εἶπεν ὁ Θεὸς, ποιησόμεθα
καὶ ἀκουσόμεθα. Καὶ οἱ ταῦτα ἐπαγγελλόμενοι, μόσχον ἄψυχον προσεκύνουν, καὶ
τὸν νεκρὸν τοῦ ζῶντος Θεοῦ προετίμων. Ἄλλο ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, τὰς
τραχυκέντρους καὶ βλασφημογλώσσους αἱρέσεις, αἵτινες τὸν τῆς εὐσεβείας σπόρον
καθ' ἡμέραν συμπνίγουσιν. Ἕτερον ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν, τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν
τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τὴν εὔφορον, τὴν καρποφοροῦσαν τριάκοντα καὶ ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἑκατόν.
Τριάκοντα τὸν τῆς σωφροσύνης ζυγόν· ἑξήκοντα τῆς ἀγγελομόρφου παρθενίας·
ἑκατὸν τῆς θείας δικαιοσύνης, καὶ ἁγνείας, καὶ τῆς τῶν μαρτύρων ἀνδραγαθίας. Οἱ
γὰρ τῆς εὐσεβείας κήρυκες τὴν ἐπ' ἐσχάτων τοῦ Κυρίου ἔλευσιν πᾶσιν
εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ἔλεγον·
Οὕτως ἐλεύσεται, ὃν τρόπον ἐθεάσασθε αὐτὸν ἀναλαμβανόμενον. Ὤφθησαν
γὰρ δύο ἄνδρες ἐν ἐσθῆτι λευκῇ. ∆ύο, ἵνα πιστευθῇ ἡ ἀλήθεια· ἄνδρες, ἵνα εἰς
ἀνδρίαν τοὺς μαθητὰς στηρίξωσι· λευχειμονοῦντες, ἵνα καταλαμπρύνωσι τὰς τῶν
ἀκουόντων διανοίας. Τί οὖν οἱ ὀφθέντες ἐκήρυττον; Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, τί ἑστήκατε
βλέποντες εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; τί εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀτενίζετε; Μᾶλλον τὸν οὐρανοῦ
ποιητὴν θεωροῦντες, δοξάσατε τοῦ ἀναλαμβανομένου τὸ μέγεθος, καὶ τὴν
συγκατάβασιν αὐτοῦ τῆς φιλανθρωπίας θαυμάσατε, ὅτι τὸν γήινον ἑνώσας ἑαυτῷ
ἄνθρωπον, οὐρανοπολίτην ἀνέδειξε, καὶ οἰκήτορα οὐρανοῦ κατέστησε· βαβαί! τὸν
κάτω κείμενον ποῦ ἀνήγαγε.
Τί ἑστήκατε βλέποντες εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; Οὕτως ἐλεύσεται. Οὕτω. Πῶς; Τὸ
σῶμα τὸ ἡμέτερον περικείμενος, τὴν τρωθεῖσαν τῇ λόγχῃ πλευρὰν προβαλλόμενος·
ἵνα ὄψωνται οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι εἰς ὃν ἐξεκέντησαν· ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀξιωθῶμεν ὄψεσθαι τὸ
πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ μετὰ παῤῥησίας, καὶ τῶν ἐπηγγελμένων ἀγαθῶν ἐπιτύχωμεν·
χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· μεθ' οὗ τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ ἁγίῳ
Πνεύματι δόξα, κράτος, τιμὴ, νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ, καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The good soil bears fruit and he will come again in the body
orientation: Epiphanius the preacher is closing the homily by applying the parable of the sower to the Church and repeating what the two men in white announced about Christ's return.
pass_a_gloss: But as a guard having the eye of the soul sleepless, do not allow the robber to break through the eye of the mind, in order that being confident you may say to him: Betrayer of a master's property I do not become, devil. For of the Lord is the earth and the Church of Christ which is always cultivated by the heavenly rain, and bearing fruit to Christ always fresh, thirty and sixty and a hundred. The sower went out, he says, to sow; and one part fell upon the way, the Greek deception. And the birds came, the plunderers of the demons keen in hunger, and devoured it. Another fell upon the rocky places, the purpose of the Jews hard in manner I mean, and immediately sprang up a plant of rashness and of lawlessness. For such is the manner of the Jews. For while being given law in the desert they kept saying to Moses: All things as many as God has said, we will do and we will hear. And the ones promising these things were worshipping a calf without soul, and were honoring the dead thing above the living God. Another fell upon the thorns, the heresies rough with spikes and blasphemous in tongue, which choke the seed of piety day by day. A different seed fell upon the good earth, the Church of Christ, the fruitful, the one bearing fruit thirty and sixty and a hundred. Thirty the yoke of self control; sixty of the virginity having the form of an angel; a hundred of the divine righteousness, and of purity, and of the brave deed of the martyrs. For the heralds of piety proclaiming the good news to all of the coming of the Lord at the last times were saying: In this way he will come, in which manner you beheld him being taken up. For two men were seen in white clothing. Two, in order that the truth may be believed; men, in order that they may strengthen the disciples into manliness; wearing white, in order that they may make bright the minds of the hearers. What therefore were the ones who were seen proclaiming? Men who are Israelites, why have you stood looking into heaven? why do you gaze intently into heaven? Rather while beholding the maker of heaven, glorify the greatness of the one being taken up, and wonder at the coming down of his love for humanity, because having united to himself the human from earth, he showed him forth a citizen of heaven, and made him a dweller of heaven; O wonder! the one lying below to where did he lead him up. Why have you stood looking into heaven? In this way he will come. In this way. How? Wearing our body around him, holding before him the side wounded by the spear; in order that the Jews may see him whom they pierced; but that we may be counted worthy to behold his face with boldness, and may attain the promised good things; by grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ; with whom to the Father and to the holy Spirit be glory, might, honor, now and always, and into the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: Prohibition in second person, addressed to the hearer guarding the mind, not a wish or general statement.
Present statement of refusal to act as betrayer of what belongs to the master, keeping who does what.
Purpose clause: the men strengthen disciples so as to stand firm in courage, not merely give support.

choices.english: holding before him the side wounded by the spear
choices.why: Present participle of display: he presents the wounded side as evidence at his coming.
Manner of seeing his face openly and confidently, not private speech.

pass_b_english: But keep watch like a guard with a sleepless eye for your soul. Do not allow the robber to break through the eye of your mind, so that you can say to him with boldness, “I am no betrayer of my Master’s property, devil. For the earth is the Lord’s (Psalm 24:1), and so is Christ’s Church, tilled at all times by the rain from heaven and bearing fresh fruit for Christ thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”

“A sower went out to sow,” Scripture says (Matthew 13:3). Some seed fell on the road, which is Greek deception. Then the birds came, the ravenous demon plunderers, and devoured it. Other seed fell on rocky ground, which, I mean, is the hard-hearted resolve of the Jews, and at once a growth of recklessness and lawlessness shot up. Such, indeed, is the way of the Jews. For while they were receiving the law in the desert, they said to Moses, “All that God has said, we will do and we will hear” (Exodus 24:7). Yet the very men who promised this worshiped a lifeless calf and set a dead thing above the living God.

Other seed fell among thorns, which are the rough-spined and foul-mouthed heresies that choke the seed of piety day after day. But other seed fell on the good soil, which is Christ’s fruitful Church, bearing fruit thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold. Thirtyfold is the yoke of self-control, sixtyfold is angel-like virginity, and a hundredfold is divine righteousness and purity and the brave deeds of the martyrs.

The heralds of piety proclaimed the Lord’s coming at the end to all, saying, “He will come in the same way you saw him ascending” (Acts 1:11). For two men appeared in white clothing (Acts 1:10). Two, so that the truth would be believed; men, to strengthen the disciples into manliness; in white, to flood the minds of their hearers with light. What, then, did those who appeared proclaim? “Men of Israel, why do you stand looking into heaven? Why do you gaze into the sky? Look instead on the Maker of heaven, glorify the greatness of him who is ascending, and marvel at his coming down in love for humanity. For he united the earthly man to himself and made him a citizen of heaven and a dweller in heaven. O wonder, where he has lifted up the one who lay below!”

Why do you stand looking into heaven? He will come in this way. In what way? He will come wearing our body and holding before him the side wounded by the spear, so that the Jews will see him whom they pierced (John 19:37). And may we be counted worthy to see his face with boldness and to obtain the promised goods, by the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom be glory, might, and honor to the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
notes: Bracketed [καὶ ἑξήκοντα] and [καὶ] are editorial uncertainty; glossed with and retained in brackets.
